children: Cerity Partners is expanding its presence in its home market of New York City with the addition of the Contant-Leit and Wacht Groups, two financial advisor teams that oversaw a total of $1.4 billion in client assets with Shufro Rose. The advisors are expected to join Cerity Sept. 30.

The teams will boost the advisor roster and assets of Cerity, one of the nation's largest independent registered investment advisor firms. Cerity Partners was ranked the No. 8 Mega RIA on Barron's 2026 Top 100 RIA Firms and has $161.7 billion of assets under management, according to its most recent Form ADV filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Both teams are led by industry veterans and cater to a loyal client base that includes multigenerational families. Their average client relationship has lasted 21 years, according to Cerity.

"Their deep, multigenerational client relationships, commitment to their colleagues, and their presence in New York will strengthen our ability to serve individuals, families, and businesses," says Claire O'Keefe, Cerity's head of partner development.

The Contant-Leit Group is led by John Contant and Stephen Leit. Contant joined Shufro Rose in 1996 and first registered as an investment advisor with the firm in 2007. Leit joined the firm in 1984 and registered as an advisor in 1989. Shufro Rose didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on the moves.
The Contant-Leit practice offers investment management and other services, including retirement and estate planning, tax advice, and family education.

Contant says that joining an enterprise with Cerity's scale will enable his team to enhance its service model, providing clients with a wider range of investments and specialized guidance. "As a part of Cerity Partners, our clients will receive the same personalized guidance from the same trusted team, now backed by a broader set of resources, expertise, and capabilities to help them achieve even more," he says.

The Wacht Group is led by industry veteran Harvey Wacht, whose practice offers financial planning as well as tax, estate, and legacy planning. Wacht first registered as a broker in 1970 with Kenneth Bove & Co. After stints with a few other firms he joined Shufro Rose as a broker and investment advisor in 2001, according to registration records.

The latest recruiting wins from Cerity follow last week's announcement that it is bringing onboard Gilbert & Cook, an Iowa advisor firm with about $2 billion in assets under management. That acquisition is expected to close at the end of the month.
